relevance_note: Family study describing two homozygous Tangier patients and their heterozygous relatives individually: 'Patient J. S., homozygous for Tangier disease'.
method_note: 1977 family study (S. family) of Tangier disease heterozygotes; no gene or variant is named anywhere (pre-ABCA1), so the variants table is empty: the paper ties no ABCA1 variant to anyone. In scope: the two homozygous propositi (J. S., E. G.; diagnosis of Tangier disease) and relatives described in relation to them. Table III rows use the paper's pedigree labels; its rows were read by a short script (cells checked by eye). Table III VIII 11 (female, 79) and VIII 12 (male, 79) are treated as the mother and father of the propositi, because the text says the two obligate heterozygous parents are both 79 and Table III's obligate group is 'children and parents of propositi'; text facts about the parents (79, good health, no CAD/PVD, German ancestry) were attached to them, and the mother's rectal biopsy to VIII 11 (only obligate heterozygote in the biopsy list). X 5 is the one biopsied relative not in Table III, presumably the 'unaffected close relative', but the paper does not say so; no features recorded for X 5. M. G. and R. S. (obligate heterozygotes in Figs 4-6) and 'sister of propositi' (HDL 29-42 mg/dl over 12 months, oral contraceptives) get their own rows, but they may be the same people as Table III rows (M. G. possibly VIII 11 or one of X 15-X 19; the sister possibly IX 26 or IX 35); the paper gives no mapping, so they were not merged. Ages 42 and 46 of the two homozygous patients are not assigned (no mapping). Group statements used: 'total amount of HDL protein ... substantially reduced in all heterozygous patients', A apoproteins reduced ~50% in heterozygous patients, absence of hyperchylomicronemia/broad-beta/TG-rich LDL in 'any of the heterozygous patients' (hypertriglyceridemia present 'in a few instances', unnamed, so not reported), normal LDL amounts in heterozygous patients (text is column-interleaved; two fragments quoted), the five presumed heterozygotes' low HDL cholesterol, low Apo A-I and rectal lipid storage, and no CAD/PVD in the two homozygous and two parental heterozygous patients; these were applied to the 12 Table III heterozygotes only. Low HDL cholesterol was not marked for the obligate heterozygotes: the paper says heterozygote HDL cholesterol may fall within the normal range. 'Peripheral vascular disease' excluded does not exclude the broader non-coronary atherosclerosis checklist item. Table III sex 'female§' (IX 26) has an undefined footnote. Contradictions: Methods says 'eight obligate heterozygous patients' but Results and Table III have seven; text gives the mother's HDL cholesterol as 39 mg/dl and children/parents' range 27-39, while Table III gives VIII 11 34 mg/dl and the obligate range 23-34 (different samplings likely). Publication year is not printed (received 1977). The OCR text is column-interleaved in places.
